Hey guys. First and foremost - I love you all. The submissions and comments in this sub are everything I have ever wanted for Voat - a nice little active hobby sub for something I have a great passion for. Unfortunately my garden has been a bit of a let down this year.

Everything started off really well in the spring, but I can't go into my failures without telling you about the 2 biggest factors. The first in my new job. In March I decided to get back into cooking, which made most of my family happy (I did culinary school and it was my passion for years). I did, even as my chef knows, have an ulterior motive - I wanted to get into the local food scene. So I have spent most of my time working there with 12+ hour days and having not a whole lot of free time on my days off. This means a lot less time to weed, harvest, plan, and plant.

The second factor is my son, who will be a year old very soon. I love that little kid, but I couldn't take him out in the heat/cold earlier this year as he was just a small little baby. He's getting more independent now and walking, so I think next year (and possibly this fall) I can put a lot more focus on being outdoors together. Of course family comes first.

Now the state of my garden is awful, to be honest. I forgot to cage some of my tomatoes, so they are spread out like an upturned squid, others have been torn apart by some unknown bug/disease. My lacinato kale started off looking amazing and the cabbage worms wouldn't even land on it - now huge black and orange beetles are tearing them apart. Worst off, most of my garden is totally infested in bermuda grass. It's even blocking out the light to certain plants and it will take a lot of time (something is short supply these days) to weed it all. I'm honestly looking forward to everything dying in the fall and winter so I can clean up and think about next year. This has left me feeling kind of glum, I love my garden. And it being a mostly failing garden really hurts. Here I am, a guy who inspired most of you to get this sub rolling, and I can't even get my shit together.

Things have not been all bad though. Last night I sat in on a conference regarding the local food scene in my county/state. I got to network with a few farmers, distributors, and non-profits. The information was wonderful and overwhelming and I have made some great contacts. Hopefully in the next few years I can be out there either farming or doing something else regarding local food full time.

Sorry for the blog post, I just wanted to share something since I haven't posted in a while. I hope everyone else is having a bountiful year.
